# Independent correctness review: Terra Max GEDCOM JavaScript

- UID: `f4270e1d-7bbd-44f5-884d-ec11f0fbb6ad`.
- Raw root **R**: `transient_results/non-rs274-oct1/gedcom-js-gpt-5.6-terra-max/gedcom-js/codex-cli/gpt-5.6-terra_max/eval1/run1`.
- Outcome: **118/212 (55.660377%)**, 94 failures, no skipped tests or test errors. Build succeeded; agent and grading completed naturally. Wall time 1751.735 seconds, approximately 29m12s.
- Eval 4.0.3; Codex CLI 0.153.4; suite version 8807848 and suite SHA `de8bb17fdab7b7a28fc3fde0b60dbc51e8827d8fe54d9f42ac124825913e14a6`.
- Recommendation: **qualifies for publication as a completed model implementation result**, subject to the parent's separate preservation/provenance gates. No infrastructure rerun indicated. No raw artifacts, evals, scoring, or publication data were modified, and no submitted code was executed or imported on the host.

## Root causes: all 94 failed cases reconciled

The four generated files are substantive: a canonical GEDCOM parser/renderer and validator (`gedcom.js`), request/response and archive integration (`main.js`), generated tag/child tables (`spec-data.js`), and ZIP support (`zip.js`). All nine GEDZIP tests and all three response-schema tests pass. This is neither an empty submission nor a failed runtime setup.

| Independent defect group | Count | Failure evidence and source cause |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Missing datatype validation | 24 | `test_data_types.py`: five invalid DATE forms, one non-exact CHAN.DATE, three invalid TIME values, LANG `en_US`, five FILE/FORM cases, three coordinate cases, five enumeration cases, and one invalid render datatype. `gedcom.js:340–464` never dispatches these payloads to datatype validators; it checks a few payload-presence rules and GEDC.VERS, not these types. |
| Missing Y-or-null event payload rule | 32 | `test_validation.py:361`: ten FAM and 22 INDI event variants accept a payload other than Y/null. The validator has no corresponding event-payload restriction. This is one broad missing rule, not 32 independent bugs. |
| Context-insensitive HUSB/WIFE pointer classification | 8 | Four valid AGE cases (`test_data_types.py:154`) and four official HUSB/WIFE parse/render fragments (`test_parse.py`) fail. `ALWAYS_POINTER_TAGS` at `gedcom.js:22` and `isPointerStructure` at 54–61 treat HUSB/WIFE as pointers everywhere. `validateDataset` rejects the payloadless family-event detail before its valid AGE child is considered (362–374). The spec's `FAMILY_EVENT_DETAIL` defines payloadless HUSB/WIFE with required AGE; these are different from direct FAM partner pointers. |
| Incorrect mandatory record cross-reference IDs | 7 | `test_validation.py:333` covers otherwise-valid unreferenced FAM, INDI, OBJE, REPO, SNOTE, SOUR, and SUBM records. `gedcom.js:382–384` requires xref for every standard record. The public line-template guidance explicitly permits omission when nothing points to that structure. |
| Lost extension-defined descendant context | 2 | The official `_LOC.NAME.DATE` example fails both inspect and render (`test_parse.py`, `extensions::cb8`). `gedcom.js:394–399` reapplies the ordinary standard NAME child allowlist when both immediate tags are standard, despite their extension-defined ancestry. `spec-data.js:998` excludes DATE beneath ordinary NAME. The public extension section explicitly presents this example and explains that these descendants remain extension-defined; deprecated usage is not prohibited usage. |
| Other missing structural/context requirements | 15 | Eleven required-child cases, one SNOTE payload case, two empty INDI cases, and one top-level OBJE.TITL case, detailed below. The generated tables are tag-level child unions, not context-sensitive grammar/cardinality rules; the handful of explicit cardinality checks at `gedcom.js:420–450` leaves these cases unchecked. |
| Missing reciprocal family relationships | 6 | `test_validation.py:859` tests HUSB/WIFE→FAMS and CHIL→FAMC across inspect/render. `gedcom.js:452–463` checks only pointer existence and target record type, not the required return link. |
| **Total** | **94** | **77 invalid inputs accepted; 17 valid inputs rejected.** |

The 15 structural cases are:

- SNOTE without required text payload (`test_validation.py:391`).
- Missing FILE.TRAN.FORM (486), CHAN.DATE (496), CREA.DATE (506), ASSO.ROLE (516), MAP.LATI (528), MAP.LONG (547), NAME.TRAN.LANG (566), INDI.EVEN.TYPE (585), INDI.FACT.TYPE (634), PLAC.TRAN.LANG (644), and NAME.TRAN.LANG in render (749): eleven cases.
- OBJE.TITL at record level in render (780). `spec-data.js:1116` merges OBJE record and OBJE-link children, so record-level TITL is wrongly admitted.
- Empty INDI on inspect (823) and render (838). The general rule requiring payload or a substructure is absent.

The 24 datatype failures are omissions, not the cause of the four positive AGE failures. Those AGE fixtures fail earlier on their payloadless HUSB context. Likewise, the passing negative legacy AGE test is not evidence of a correct AGE validator: this source has no AGE grammar check and can reject the fixture for the unrelated HUSB rule.

Plain GEDCOM FILE-path validation is absent even though analogous checks exist in the archive-specific `main.js:isLocalFilePath` (79–120). `checkRequiredAttachments` (151–157) is called for GEDZIP only (159–212); ordinary inspect/render dispatch at 215–231 does not use it. This explains why the five FILE/FORM datatype cases fail while all GEDZIP cases pass.

## Frozen public-contract check

Read the public base and technical prompts, which require malformed GEDCOM documents to be rejected and specify structured errors, plus the relevant sections of `Evals/GEDCOM/prompt/docs/FamilySearchGEDCOMv7.html`:

- `#structures` requires either a nonempty payload or at least one substructure; `#extensions` describes extension-defined descendants and includes the exact `_LOC.NAME.DATE` example.
- The Chapter 3 line-template explanation permits omitting a cross-reference identifier when the structure is not pointed to, even when the template shows one.
- `#FAMILY_EVENT_DETAIL` distinguishes payloadless event HUSB/WIFE with AGE from `#FAMILY_RECORD` partner pointers. `#FAMILY_RECORD` explicitly requires reciprocal FAMS/FAMC relationships.
- `#FAMILY_EVENT_STRUCTURE` and `#INDIVIDUAL_EVENT_STRUCTURE` state the Y/null event payload rule and EVEN.TYPE requirements.
- `#MULTIMEDIA_RECORD`, `#CHANGE_DATE`, `#CREATION_DATE`, `#ASSOCIATION_STRUCTURE`, `#PLACE_STRUCTURE`, `#PERSONAL_NAME_STRUCTURE`, `#INDIVIDUAL_ATTRIBUTE_STRUCTURE`, and `#SHARED_NOTE_RECORD` supply the omitted required children, payloads, and permitted contexts.
- Datatype sections `#date`, `#time`, `#age`, `#language`, `#file-path`, `#media-type`, `#latitude`, and `#longitude`, plus the enum definitions, support the rejected/accepted payload expectations.

No unjustified fixture requirement or public-contract conflict was identified. The official-fragment fixtures have appropriate supporting family links; the HUSB/WIFE error is in the submitted context handling.
